triage.why: My rule used arg(0) (the recipient) as the amount instead of arg(1); a zero-amount transfer is correct behaviour.
After assets are pushed into the vault (redeem to receiver=vault), a 1-wei deposit is accepted and mints 0 shares, so the depositor silently loses funds; deposit lacks a shares>0 check.
withdrawAll sends ETH before zeroing the balance and transfer is not nonReentrant, so the callback moves the balance elsewhere and it is then counted twice, breaking sum(balanceOf)==totalDeposits.
Same reentrancy in withdrawAll: balances transferred during the callback survive, leaving credited balances unbacked by ETH.
Because of the withdrawAll reentrancy, totalDeposits is lower than the credited balances, so an honest holder's withdrawAll underflows and their funds are stuck.
Same desync: totalDeposits underflows and an honest holder cannot withdraw a balance they legitimately hold.
modify works on a cancelled order whose amount was not zeroed, so the maker can extract base again (double refund / reopening a closed order).
Same missing active check in modify: a cancelled order can be modified and moves escrowed base again.
Anyone can send QUOTE straight to the book with a token transfer; that is an outside donation, not contract behaviour.
The depositor first set its allowance to the vault to 0, so the revert is expected; my condition left out the allowance requirement.
